extracted.intended_audience: applicants for duty-free scientific imports, institutional equipment purchasers, commodity sellers/buyers, agricultural producers, and government commodity/loan officers
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive criteria used by the Department of Commerce (Office of Scientific and Technical Equipment) and Commodity Credit Corporation for deciding applications for duty-free entry of scientific articles and for conducting CCC commodity sales and loan-extensions. Includes required application content, bases for assessing equivalence, and sale/loan procedures and price minimum rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic equivalent nonexistence
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision: 'No instrument or apparatus of equivalent scientific value to the foreign article, for the purposes for which such article is intended to be used, is being manufactured in the United States.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the controlling legal finding for approval: the Department must determine that no U.S.-manufactured instrument of equivalent scientific value exists for the intended purposes. Decisions give specific technical bases (see below) demonstrating nonequivalence (e.g., resolution, voltages, simplicity, unique design).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must state intended use
rubrics_metrics.description: Each docket entry lists: 'Intended use of article:' followed by detailed research/teaching uses (e.g., 'research projects of pathology staff, teaching medical students, interns, and residents in oncology').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated intended use frames the evaluation of equivalence—features pertinent to that use (e.g., teaching simplicity vs. high-resolution research) are given weight in the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison on technical specifications relevant to intended use
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions compare foreign article features to domestic models on the basis of specifications relevant to the stated purpose (examples: 'guaranteed resolution of 5 Angstroms' vs. domestic '8 Angstroms'; accelerating voltages of 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100 kilovolts vs. domestic 50 and 100 kilovolts; 'digital readout of the continuous fine focusing system').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department explains why particular specs are 'pertinent' to the intended use (e.g., lower voltages afford optimum contrast for thin unstained biological specimens; additional voltages permit repeatable focus for multiple students). Technical advantages that materially affect the intended purpose support approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity/usability as an evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions consider operational complexity/simplicity (e.g., foreign instrument 'relatively simple to operate, ... permits students to start the mechanism, check the alignment and operate the article after a short training period' versus domestic instrument 'complex ... requires highly qualified personnel').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where intended use is teaching or routine operations, usability and training burden are explicit grounds for distinguishing non-equivalence even if domestic instruments have higher raw technical specs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique design / non-interchangeability of spare parts
rubrics_metrics.description: For spare parts applications (e.g., Tulane University), the decision states that 'These spare parts are uniquely designed to be used with the electron microscope for which they are intended to be used' and that 'no similar spare parts ... which are interchangeable ... are being manufactured in the United States.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness and lack of interchangeability with domestically manufactured parts support approval for duty-free entry of parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record availability for public review
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the record pertaining to the decision 'is available for public review during ordinary business hours of the Department of Commerce, at the Office of Scientific and Technical Equipment, Department of Commerce, Room 5123, Washington, D.C. 20230.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must state where and when the record is available for inspection to satisfy transparency/public-review requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments considered / notice whether comments received
rubrics_metrics.description: Each docket entry includes 'Comments: No comments have been received with respect to this application.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice explicitly reports whether public comments were received and factors that may reflect on the administrative record; this is part of the procedural record for the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must identify manufacturer and country of origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application lists 'Manufacturer:' and the foreign source (e.g., 'Manufacturer: Carl Zeiss, West Germany'; 'Manufacturer: N. V. Philips ... The Netherlands').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing manufacturer and origin is required and used to identify the foreign article and compare it to available domestic products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of solicitation/ability of domestic manufacturers to supply
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions may note attempts to obtain domestic alternatives (e.g., 'The applicant’s invitation to bid on the instrument, which was sent to several domestic manufacturers, resulted in either negative replies or no response'), and conclude lack of domestic manufacturer willing to accept contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An absence of domestic bids or unwillingness of domestic firms to build the specialized instrument supports the finding that an equivalent is not being manufactured domestically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pertinence of specific features to intended purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department explains why discrete features are 'pertinent' (e.g., 'the additional resolving capabilities provided by the foreign article are pertinent', 'the additional accelerating voltages provided ... are pertinent to the purposes for which the article is intended to be used').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every technical advantage suffices—features must be linked to the stated uses to establish relevance for the equivalence determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales method: competitive offers under Announcement terms
rubrics_metrics.description: CCC disposals and sales 'Competitive offers under the terms and conditions of Announcements' (list of Announcement codes such as NO-C-6, NO-C-10, CN-EX-22, NO-C-27, NO-C-18, NO-C-20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commodity sales are conducted by competitive bidding under the specific Announcement governing that commodity or use (export, barter, restricted, unrestricted). The Announcement cited defines detailed terms and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price minimums and pricing rules set by CCC
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: 'Cotton may be acquired at its current market price, as determined by CCC, but not less than a minimum price determined by CCC which will in no event be less than 120 points (1.2 cents per pound) above the loan rate for such cotton.' For extra long staple: 'sold at the highest price offered but in no event at less than the higher of (a) 115 percent of the current support price for such cotton plus reasonable carrying charges, or (b) the domestic market price as determined by CCC.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcements and notices specify price floors and calculation rules (support price percentages, carrying charges, points above loan rate). Bidders/sellers must apply the CCC-determined floors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted vs. unrestricted use classifications and purchase limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Example for peanuts: 'Restricted-use sales. Announcement PR-1 ... terms and conditions of sales restricted to domestic crushing or export.' Further rules: 'Shelled peanuts of less than U.S. No. 1 grade may be purchased for foreign or domestic crushing.' 'Farmers stock peanuts may be purchased for domestic crushing or for export of U.S. No. 1 or better shelled peanuts. All peanuts of less than U.S. No. 1 quality must be crushed domestically.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcements/lists indicate whether lots are restricted or unrestricted and specify allowable end uses and quality-based restrictions (e.g., crushing requirements for substandard grades). Purchasers must comply with those use restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement / lot list / invitation-to-bid publication and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantities, qualities and locations are 'announced in weekly lot lists or invitations to bid' and 'Sales announcements, related forms and catalogs ... may be obtained for a nominal fee from' the named CCC offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commodity availability and sale terms are formally published in lot lists/invitations; interested buyers must consult these materials and can obtain forms/catalogs from the indicated offices (e.g., New Orleans ASCS Commodity Office, Minneapolis Branch Office).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bids submission procedures and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: All sales are made 'on the basis of competitive bids each Wednesday, by the Producer Associations Division, Agricultural Stabilization and Conservation Service, Washington, D.C. 20250, to which all bids are submitted.' For some commodities, 'Bids will include, and be evaluated on the basis of, price offered per pound f.o.b. storage location.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices specify where and when bids must be submitted (Producer Associations Division), the regular schedule (weekly Wednesday sales), and the bid evaluation basis (price f.o.b. storage or other terms stated in the Invitation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic extension of warehouse storage loans unless producer opts out in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice: 'unless the producer gives the ASC county office through which he obtained his loan written notice prior to the loan maturity date that he does not want such maturity date extended, all price support warehouse storage loans on the 1967 crops ... are extended for a period of 1 year from the original maturity date of the loans ... subject to maturity upon such earlier date as demand for payment is made.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers must give timely written notice to their ASC county office before the loan maturity date to avoid the automatic one-year extension. The notice also lists the specific new maturity dates by commodity and state groupings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified extended maturity dates by commodity and storage location
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice provides a table mapping commodities and storage-state groupings to 'From original loan maturity date' and 'To extended loan maturity date' (e.g., barley in certain states: May 31,1968 → May 31,1969; corn in all states: Apr. 30,1968 → Apr. 30,1969; soybeans in all states: June 30,1968 → June 30,1969).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers and county offices must apply the correct extension date based on commodity and location; loans remain subject to earlier demand for payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstorable processed commodities sold at not less than CCC-determined domestic market price
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonstorable items: 'At not less than domestic market price as determined by CCC.' (cited in cotton office section: 'C. Nonstorable. At not less than domestic market price as determined by CCC.')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonstorable processed commodities are priced against CCC's domestic market price floor, rather than formula floors tied to support prices or loan rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcements and codes specify detailed sale terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Sales reference specific Announcement codes (e.g., NO-C-6, NO-C-10, CN-EX-22, NO-C-27, NO-C-18, NO-C-20, PR-1, MP-14, NTOM-PR-4) 'as amended' and state 'Terms and conditions of sale are as set forth in Announcement ... and the applicable Invitation to Bid.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Announcement code is the authoritative source for detailed sale terms; notices in the Federal Register summarize but direct readers to the Announcement and Invitation for full conditions.
